entry.summary: Since 23 April 2026, non-visa nationals arriving from outside the Common Travel Area need a UK ETA, which the UK runs for Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man. Arriving from the UK, the UK ETA already covers it.
entry.max_stay: Up to 6 months as a visitor
entry.pre_arrival: Apply at gov.uk/eta/apply or the UK ETA app at least three working days before travel; £20 (about A$38 at RBA, 30 October 2026: A$1 = £0.5258).

laws.rule: Visitors may drive on a valid foreign licence for the vehicle category and should carry it; a Jersey licence is needed after 12 months or on becoming resident.

Adults 17 and over may bring 1 litre of spirits, 4 litres of wine, 16 litres of beer or cider, 200 cigarettes or 250 g tobacco and 50 ml e-liquid duty free, plus GBP 390 of other goods by commercial transport. Undeclared excess is seized with the whole allowance.

Prescribed controlled drugs may be carried in or out under an open general licence: no more than 3 months' supply (methadone 1 month), with a prescriber's letter naming the drugs, doses and travel dates. Prescribed medicinal cannabis must not be smoked or shared, and you must be able to prove the prescription at the border.

steps.step: Apply for a UK ETA on GOV.UK at least three working days before travel.
